subject: Decision criteria: latency, cost, and deployment (Finova)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@finova.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery (latency/cost/deployment)

Hi Tom —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and a set of clarifying questions so we can scope a PoC and pricing: 

Summary of what I heard: 
- Decision criteria: latency (user-facing p95), overall cost per active user/embedding workload, and ability to meet security/procurement requirements.
- Deployment preference: Finova is leaning toward Dedicated for predictable throughput but open to Hosted for a fast PoC.
- Stakeholders: Leah (economic buyer) and Pradeep (procurement) will be involved, plus SREs for technical sign-off.

Clarifying questions / asks: 
1) Latency targets: can you confirm target p95 for the user-facing product (example: 300–500ms)? Also note if there are different targets for embeddings/batch jobs.
2) QPS / concurrency estimates: can you share expected requests per second (or peak qps) and typical sequence lengths so we can size Dedicated capacity appropriately?
3) Deployment for PoC: would you prefer we run a short PoC on Hosted first (faster) or provision a small Dedicated trial (2–4 GPUs) to prove throughput/SLA?
4) Procurement timeline: any known gating items or preferred contract cadence (6–8 weeks, faster, etc.)?
5) Compliance evidence: we'll share SOC 2 + data residency details; any other required docs?

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (PoC plan), sla-summary.xlsx (SLA summary).

Proposed next steps: 
- You confirm (1) latency target and (2) qps/seq length.
- If ok, we schedule a short technical call with your SREs to collect metrics and agree PoC scope.

Thanks — I can be flexible on timing this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery (latency/cost/deployment)

Thanks Marissa — good recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

1) Latency targets: for the customer-facing feature we are targeting p95 at ~400ms end-to-end. For embeddings/batch jobs, latency is less critical; cost is the dominant factor there.
2) QPS / concurrency: initial launch expected ~150–200 RPS with spikes up to 500 RPS during peak. Typical sequence length: 80–120 tokens for chat-like flows; embeddings requests are batched and fairly large.
3) Deployment: we do want Dedicated for production due to predictable throughput and data isolation. For PoC we are open to Hosted if it gets us running in days, but if Redwood can provision a small Dedicated trial (2 GPUs) that would best reflect production performance.
4) Procurement timeline: estimate 6–8 weeks but that depends on SOW/legal review — looping procurement (Pradeep) to confirm.
5) Compliance: SOC 2 type II is required, plus proof of data residency in the US.

Looping in Leah and Pradeep — Leah will be primary economic owner and Pradeep handles procurement.

Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Product Operations, Finova
+1 415-555-0192

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery (latency/cost/deployment)

Appreciate the recap — quick context from me as the economic owner: 

Our key decision criteria are, in priority order: 
1) User experience: sustained p95 latency below ~450ms for the feature to be acceptable. Any solution that has significant tail latency will be a hard no.
2) Total cost of ownership: we need a forecasted model showing per-user/month and per-1M-embedding costs. Ballpark target is keeping inference compute under the current threshold we have for CPU-based solutions; this will require Redwood to demonstrate clear unit-cost improvements or batching efficiencies.
3) Security & procurement: SOC 2 and data-residency are hard requirements.

About deployment: if a Dedicated trial is possible for PoC, that is preferred. However, for speed to evaluate model quality and integration we can start with Hosted for two weeks and then spin up Dedicated for throughput validation.

Happy to join the technical call — please include SREs and a couple of engineering leads.

-Leah
Leah Morgan
Chief Product Officer, Finova

Hi Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks for looping procurement in. Attached is our procurement intake (finova-procurement-intake.pdf) which includes standard contract terms, security checklist, and expected procurement cadence. A few items we need from Redwood to move forward: 
- SOC 2 Type II report (latest) and point of contact for security questions.
- Confirmation of data residency options (we require US-only processing for PII in this workload).
- Draft SOW or PoC statement of work, and proposed pricing for Dedicated trial vs Hosted PoC.

Our estimated procurement timeline assuming no major legal exceptions is 6–8 weeks after we receive SOC2 and the PoC SOW. If you can share SOC2 and a short SOW (1–2 pages) by EOD Monday, we can start internal review.

Thanks — Pradeep
